subject: Reconciliation: who absorbs correspondent bank commission on EUR remittance?
content:
--- Message 1/5 ---
From: treasurer@acmehealth.com (Marta Ruiz)
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on EUR payout - bank deducted intermediary fee

Hi Sean,

We received the EUR payout for INV-4829 (USD invoice paid by Acme on 2026-05-15) but the beneficiary got EUR 14.85 less than expected. Our bank (FinBank) says an intermediary correspondent took EUR 14.85 as a commission. The invoice was paid net-of-fees per our prior chats, but it looks like the remittance path included an extra correspondent.

Can you confirm how Redwood presents the invoice (gross vs net), and whether Acme or Redwood should absorb that intermediary commission? Also, can you provide the MT103/trace so we can reconcile on our side?

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Treasurer, Acme Health
attachments: INV-4829.pdf

--- Message 2/5 ---
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: treasurer@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-18 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discrepancy on EUR payout - bank deducted intermediary fee

Forwarding Marta's note. In short: Acme paid USD amount per invoice; our payment rail converted and sent EUR to their IBAN. Their bank reports a correspondent commission was deducted en route (EUR 14.85).

Questions for ops/legal:
- Do we bill Acme gross (showing bank commission line item) or invoice net and treat the commission as a customer liability?
- If customer is responsible, do we need to change wire instructions to indicate "sender pays all intermediaries" or include intermediary coverage language?
- If Redwood absorbs, how do we recover/expense the FX P&L and show it on accounting?

Attachments: INV-4829.pdf, wire_template_sample.xlsx

-- Sean Gallagher
Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
--- Message 3/5 ---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: treasurer@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-18 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discrepancy on EUR payout - bank deducted intermediary fee

Thanks for flagging. Quick notes from finance ops:

1) Current default: our invoices state amounts due in invoice currency (USD). When customers elect to send in local currency we treat it as a full payment only if the beneficiary receives the full USD-equivalent net. Historically we have required customers to instruct their banks "OUR" cover (ordering bank pays all fees) or use the Swift field to indicate beneficiary should receive full amount.

2) If the bank chain deducts an intermediary fee, two practical approaches:
   - Option A (Customer covers): Ask Acme to re-issue payment with ordering bank covering all correspondent fees (preferred). We can add explicit language to the invoice and wire template.
   - Option B (Redwood covers): We absorb the EUR 14.85, record as bank commission expense, and credit Acme on next invoice or issue a one-off credit. This is simple but sets a precedent.

3) For reconciliation we need the MT103/Swift trace plus the beneficiary bank's claim showing the correspondent deduction. Marta, can FinBank share an MT103 PDF? We can match UETR/transaction reference (we have our Payment ID: RW-20260515-ACME-4829).

Proposed immediate action: ask customer to confirm whether they'll re-send with "ordering bank covers" for future payments and request the MT103 for this transaction so ops can book the expense or raise a small credit.

Ben Carter
Sr. Payments Ops | Redwood Inference
--- Message 4/5 ---
From: treasurer@acmehealth.com (Marta Ruiz)
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: payments-ops@finbank.com
Date: 2026-05-18 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on EUR payout - bank deducted intermediary fee

Thanks, Ben. FinBank attached the MT103 PDF and their trace reference; I've included payments-ops@finbank.com on this thread. They confirm: remittance used an intermediary bank due to correspondent routing on our bank's side. They also say their standard guidance is to set the ordering bank to cover "ALL" intermediaries; our payment should have been sent as OUR-pay.

Happy to re-send if Redwood needs us to, but since this was a one-off vendor payout during our month-end, we prefer Redwood either: (a) issue a small credit of EUR 14.85 and move on, or (b) show bank commission as a separate line for transparency and have Acme cover future intermediary fees.

Attached: MT103-sample.pdf

Marta
--- Message 5/5 ---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, treasurer@acmehealth.com, payments-ops@finbank.com
Date: 2026-05-18 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on EUR payout - bank deducted intermediary fee

Marta / FinBank / Sean / Ben — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Operational decision and policy guidance below: 

Short answer: we will credit Acme EUR 14.85 for this specific transaction and update our invoice/wire template going forward.

Details / next steps:
- Action 1 (current tx): Redwood will issue an invoice credit equal to the correspondent commission (EUR 14.85) against INV-4829; finance will post as "bank commission expense" and flag as non-recurring P&L. Expect a credit note (CN-4829-1) within 3 business days.
- Action 2 (future payments): Update our public wire template and invoice footnote to request ordering-bank coverage for correspondent fees and include language: "If intermediaries deduct fees, the ordering bank is responsible to reimburse the beneficiary. For guaranteed receipt, please instruct your bank to set charges to OUR or to use the supplied USD nostro account." We'll attach a revised wire_template_sample.xlsx to invoices for EU customers.
- Action 3 (traceability): Ben — please confirm Redwood's standard Payment ID placement in Swift fields (we should include RW-<date>-<acct>-<inv> in field 70) so customers and correspondent banks can match MT103s.

Marta — please send the FinBank MT103 to payments-ops@redwood.ai (ops inbox) and we'll reconcile and issue the credit. If Acme chooses to re-pay grossly instead, we'll flag and settle per preference.

This approach keeps the relationship simple and avoids blocking their month-end. We'll treat this as a one-off exception; if we see repeated intermediaries charging, we'll move to stricter wire instruction enforcement.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: wire_template_sample.xlsx

--- End of thread ---
